Treat the impact number as the same result as post-bend crack observation.
reasons: Applying results requires checking conditions and use.
Losing conditions also loses a valid comparison basis.
Check the comparison assumptions, including specimen and temperature.
Results serving different evaluation purposes are not the same quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-06-q10.stem: A dial indicator mounting is loose and does not return to the same reference indication. What should be done?
options: Copy the previous good part’s value.
Read only the long hand and ignore reference changes.
Zero it separately on every part so every difference is zero.
Check mounting, movement and reference under the procedure and report affected readings.
reasons: Do not substitute values unsupported by measurement.
An unstable reference makes differences unreliable.
Arbitrary part-by-part zeroing destroys comparative meaning.
Reference stability and effects on already measured parts must be checked.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-06-q11.stem: A bore-setting ring is needed; the shelf has master and limit rings. What should be checked?
options: Check purpose, identity, reference size and inspection state; select the specified master.
Every ring shape serves the same role.
Choose only by readable engraving.
Ignore inspection status if nominal size is close.
reasons: Verify the reference role and condition, not shape alone.
Master and limit gauges have different purposes.
Engraving readability alone does not establish suitability.
The condition of the reference supporting comparison also matters.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-06-q12.stem: An instruction applies the smooth-hole insertion rule uniformly to a thread NO-GO gauge. What should happen?
options: Tighten hard and record only where it stops.
Confirm the entry or turn-count criteria specified for that thread and gauge.
Using GO makes all NO-GO instructions unnecessary.
Damage the thread until it stops and accept it.
reasons: Forcing threads causes damage and false judgment.
Check thread-specific criteria rather than transferring smooth-hole rules unconditionally.
GO alone cannot replace prescribed checks of both sides.
Never create acceptance by damaging the part.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q01.stem: You need to examine how equipment is positioned at a new installation site. Which drawing should you check first as suited to this purpose?
options: Only a detail drawing
A layout drawing
Only a list of lettering heights
A note containing only extracted hole dimensions
reasons: Information for machining individual parts alone cannot establish the installation arrangement.
Its function is suited to showing installation positions and similar information.
A table of lettering sizes does not show the machine layout.
The note loses information from the drawings that are needed.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q02.stem: In a third-angle drawing, from which direction is the object seen in the top view placed above the front view?
options: From below
From the right
From the left
From above
reasons: This is different from viewing from below.
The view from the right corresponds to the right-side view.
The view from the left is not the top view.
In third-angle projection, the top view seen from above is placed above the front view.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q03.stem: In a sectional view of a hollow part, you notice diagonal lines on the cut material. Which interpretation is appropriate?
options: Treat them as hatching representing the cut material, distinct from the hole space.
Always machine diagonal grooves at that location.
Every area with diagonal lines is an air passage.
Conclude that the actual object has already been cut.
reasons: The diagonal lines indicate such features as the cut surface of material.
This confuses hatching with groove-machining instructions.
This reverses the meaning of material and space.
A sectional view is an imaginary-cut representation, not a record of the actual object’s history.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q04.stem: A drawing whose unit of length is mm has a dimension 24 and an angle 24°. What is the appropriate treatment?
options: Record both as a length of 24 mm.
Record both as 24 degrees.
Record length 24 mm and angle 24 degrees separately.
Treat a length without a unit symbol as impossible to measure.
reasons: This ignores the angular unit.
This ignores the specified length unit.
The same number has a different meaning depending on its unit and feature.
Ordinary drawings may specify a common unit rather than repeating it for each dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q05.stem: A note for a part contains R8 and φ8. How should you read them without confusing the requirements?
options: Treat both as diameter 8.
Treat both as plate thickness 8.
Copy R8 as diameter 16 and erase the original symbol.
Distinguish R8 as radius 8 and φ8 as diameter 8.
reasons: This mistakes the radius indicated by R for a diameter.
These are not plate-thickness indications.
Even if conversion is possible, do not replace the original indication and its role without authorization.
Radius and diameter symbols have different meanings.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q06.stem: A drawing specifies “parallelism 0.08, datum B.” What needs checking when preparing to measure?
options: Write only 0.08 and omit the feature.
Identify the surface or axis concerned and reference B.
Use an easy-to-hold surface as a new reference.
If the length is within tolerance, consider the parallelism checked too.
reasons: The value alone does not tell you what to evaluate.
The geometrical characteristic, feature, value and reference must be considered together.
This changes the specified reference without authorization.
Meeting a dimensional tolerance alone does not guarantee parallelism.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q07.stem: Two surfaces of the same part have Ra and Rz indications. What should you do when copying them into an inspection record?
options: Change both to Ra if the numbers are close.
Use the largest value for every surface.
Retain each parameter name and value with its corresponding surface.
Record both as describing the surface colour.
reasons: This replaces different parameters without authorization.
This ignores the requirements for each surface.
Keep the parameter and its association with the relevant surface.
Ra and Rz are surface-roughness parameters.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q08.stem: The decimal point of a dimension is illegible on a copied detail drawing. What is the appropriate action before machining?
options: Put the relevant machining on hold and confirm the value on a legible approved drawing.
Choose whichever value seems larger.
Use a ruler measurement of the paper line as the official value.
Copy a number from a drawing of a different part with similar-looking lettering.
reasons: Confirm the unknown requirement rather than guessing.
A guess based on appearance does not confirm the requirement.
This cannot replace the stated dimension.
A drawing for a different object cannot establish this requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q09.stem: You are looking for the side view seen from the right on a drawing marked as third-angle projection. Where should you look in the basic arrangement?
options: Assume it is to the left of the front view.
Assume it is above the front view.
To the right of the front view.
On the reverse of the sheet.
reasons: This reverses the viewing direction and placement.
In the basic arrangement this is the top-view position.
Third-angle projection places the right-side view to the right of the front view.
This does not describe the basic arrangement of projection views.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q10.stem: Different dimensions are repeated for the same feature. What is the appropriate way for the machining worker to proceed?
options: Choose whichever value is easier to measure.
Point out the conflict and ask which dimension applies.
Keep only the larger number and correct the drawing.
Machine to the average of the two numbers.
reasons: This chooses a requirement for convenience.
Confirm the official requirement instead of choosing on your own.
This is a change without approval.
The average is not an approved requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q11.stem: You are copying the parenthesized dimension (18) from a drawing into an inspection sheet. What is appropriate?
options: Keep the parentheses and reference-dimension role, and check the instructions underlying the acceptance decision.
Erase the parentheses and make it an official acceptance criterion.
Always treat 18 as the hole depth.
Consider all other drawing instructions unnecessary because there are parentheses.
reasons: Distinguish a reference value from the basis for machining and acceptance.
This changes the dimension’s role without authorization.
Parentheses do not mean hole depth.
Other requirements are still necessary even when a reference dimension is given.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-07-q12.stem: In the welding notation used in this textbook, a basic symbol is above the reference line. What is an appropriate reading before actual work?
options: Decide that only the arrow side is to be welded.
Assume the edge preparation and weld dimensions can be chosen freely.
Treat the line as indicating a surface-roughness value.
Read it as an other-side indication and also check the applicable standard and components.
reasons: This is the opposite of the textbook’s above-line indication.
Reading the position does not authorize omission of the other instructions.
This confuses the welding reference line with a surface-texture indication.
In the textbook, above the reference line means the other side; an actual drawing also requires checking its standard.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q01.stem: A spanner is loose on a hex bolt. What should you check first?
options: Only the bolt colour.
Only the operator’s grip strength.
How to extend its handle.
The width across flats and the tool size and wear.
reasons: Colour does not indicate the fitting size.
Grip strength alone cannot identify a mismatched tool.
Extra leverage does not resolve an unsuitable tool.
Check a sound tool that fits the width across flats.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q02.stem: Which tool makes an internal thread in a chassis?
options: Flat file
Tap
Die
Scriber
reasons: It hand-finishes flat surfaces and similar areas.
A tap cuts an internal thread inside a drilled hole.
A die cuts external threads.
It marks positions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q03.stem: A comparison dial indicator with 0.01 mm divisions moves four divisions from the reference. What is the magnitude of the difference?
options: 0.4 mm
4 mm
reasons: This is ten times too large.
This treats the number of divisions as millimetres.
This is ten times too small.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q04.stem: Which instrument measures magnetic flux density near a magnet?
options: Lux meter
Height gauge
Gaussmeter
Thermocouple thermometer
reasons: It measures illuminance, a different quantity.
It measures height above a reference surface.
It measures magnetic flux density.
It measures temperature.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q05.stem: Which check is appropriate when selecting a tapping drill diameter?
options: Consult the specified table matching thread diameter, pitch, material and machining method.
Change it by visual estimate each time.
Simply apply force without drilling a hole.
Always use the nominal thread diameter for every material.
reasons: Use tables and procedures suited to the required conditions.
This does not provide controlled machining conditions.
This ignores preparation for normal tapping.
The hole diameter is not the nominal thread diameter itself.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q06.stem: What is the basic action for an ordinary metalworking file?
options: Apply strong force only on the return stroke.
Always apply equally strong force in both directions.
Cut only by twisting sideways.
Apply force on the forward stroke and release it on return.
reasons: This opposes the usual cutting direction.
This does not distinguish cutting from return.
This is not the basic cutting action described.
This matches the forward-cutting principle.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q07.stem: In a point-charge model with unchanged charge and medium, the separation triples. What fraction of the original force remains?
options: 3 times
9 times
reasons: Increasing distance does not increase the force.
This applies the square in the opposite direction.
The inverse-square relation gives 1/3² = 1/9.
This confuses inverse square with inverse distance.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q08.stem: The specified plain washers are missing. What should you do?
options: Use another washer shape without permission.
Report the part number and shortage, and confirm the specified assembly.
Increase torque instead of using washers.
Omit them to keep the appearance consistent.
reasons: The substitution has not been checked.
A specific shortage report leads to an authorized response.
Tightening torque cannot replace a washer.
This departs from the specified assembly.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q09.stem: Which statement describes a surface plate correctly?
options: Dirt cannot affect the reference.
It displays every dimension merely by placing a part on it.
It provides a reference plane for measurement or assembly.
It is necessarily an instrument for reading hole depth.
reasons: Foreign matter affects measurement posture or the reference.
A surface plate is not itself a dimensional display.
Its role is to provide a reference plane.
This confuses a surface plate with a depth instrument.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q10.stem: When replacing a thermocouple with another product, what should be checked?
options: Compatibility of type, polarity, leads, instrument setting and operating range.
Nothing: every product has the same temperature range.
Polarity is irrelevant if colours look similar.
All temperature sensors use the same instrument setting.
reasons: Check compatibility throughout the measurement system.
Operating conditions and product specifications differ.
Correct connection and polarity must be checked.
Sensor type must match the setting.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q11.stem: A hand tap suddenly becomes hard to turn. What is the best decision?
options: Move to the next hole without recording the abnormality.
Avoid forcing it; check the pilot hole, tool, lubrication and chips.
Add a long bar and always turn it through.
Release the workpiece and hold it by hand.
reasons: The unresolved abnormality may recur.
Prioritize finding the cause to prevent breakage.
This increases the risk of tool breakage.
This removes secure workpiece holding.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-06-q12.stem: Which rule determines the force direction on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
options: The rule for a file’s cutting direction.
Fleming’s right-hand rule.
A rule using only point-charge distance.
Fleming’s left-hand rule.
reasons: This is not an electromagnetic-force rule.
The right hand concerns induced electromotive force from conductor motion.
That alone cannot determine this force direction.
It determines force direction from field and current.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q01.stem: The jig shelf is in the correct location, but a jig from another process is mixed in. Which of the three fixed rules particularly needs checking?
options: Increase only the stored quantity to resolve the mix-up.
No check is needed if the shelf is the same.
Verify the designated item against the actual item.
Remove identification labels to make them uniform.
reasons: Increasing quantity does not remove the wrong item.
Both location and item must be specified.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Losing labels increases mix-ups.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q02.stem: Before improvement, 10 of 200 items were defective; afterward, 4 of 80. Which comparison is appropriate?
options: Both defect rates are 5%; counts alone do not demonstrate improvement.
Fewer defective items necessarily means the rate is less than half.
The later defect rate is 20%.
The denominator is irrelevant to quality assessment.
reasons: This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Different totals require comparing rates too.
Omitting the total examined leads to mistaken comparison.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q03.stem: You know the measurement procedure, but the target lot and frequency are unclear. What should you check?
options: Decide once daily from memory.
Check the control plan, such as the QC process chart, with the responsible person.
Always select only easy-to-measure products.
Change frequency according to operator preference.
reasons: The current plan must be checked.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
The designated targets cannot be ignored.
Control changes need prescribed approval.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q04.stem: You want to investigate treatment time and coating thickness using paired values for each product. Which tool is suitable?
options: Only one average with process order removed.
A jig storage layout.
A Pareto chart containing only counts by defect type.
A scatter diagram.
reasons: One average does not show the relationship between two variables.
Storage management differs from this analysis purpose.
Counts by type do not represent paired time and thickness values.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q05.stem: Which statement about zinc plating protecting iron is appropriate?
options: Zinc never corrodes in any environment.
Zinc can protect iron by corroding preferentially and is itself consumed.
A protective film always remains forever.
Zinc and paint have exactly the same protection mechanism.
reasons: Zinc also corrodes depending on the environment.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Protection depends on environment and coating condition.
Distinguish barrier protection from sacrificial action.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q06.stem: An ideal resistor in a paper exercise carries 15mA at 60mV. What is its resistance?
reasons: Align prefixes before calculation.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Resistance is voltage divided by current.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q07.stem: What is the equivalent resistance of positive finite 6Ω and 3Ω resistors in parallel?
reasons: This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
9Ω is the series sum.
Divide the product by the sum.
It is not the simple average of the resistances.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q08.stem: What is the best way to report an unreadable container label?
options: Identify the contents by smell before reporting.
Report only a guess that someone is at fault.
Pour it into a drain as tidying and finish reporting.
State the container location and observed facts, separating them from unconfirmed causes.
reasons: Smelling is dangerous and cannot establish identity.
Separate assumptions from observations.
Do not discard unknown chemicals without permission.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q09.stem: Defects increased after a material-lot change. What is appropriate in a 4M investigation?
options: Record the material change as a possible factor and also check factual changes in people, equipment and methods.
The material is proven to be the cause; no other check is needed.
Delete change records after seeing results.
Skip inspection to prioritize the deadline.
reasons: This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Matching timing does not prove causation.
Keep records needed for traceability.
This compromises QCDS safety and quality.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q10.stem: The applicable work standard and QC process chart conflict. What should you do?
options: Choose whichever is convenient.
Prioritize old memories over official instructions.
Check applicability and revisions, then ask the responsible person for clarification.
Rewrite documents without permission and proceed.
reasons: Do not resolve conflicts on your own.
Check currently valid documents.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Follow the prescribed change procedure.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q11.stem: A control-chart point is inside the control limits. What caution is appropriate?
options: All products are proven within specification.
Correlation in a scatter diagram always proves causation.
Abnormal values may be deleted before display.
Control limits differ from product specification limits and do not mean every product passes.
reasons: Separate process monitoring from product conformity assessment.
Association alone does not identify the cause.
Retain accurate data.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.

mfg1-surface-weekly-06-q12.stem: Ideal 4Ω and 8Ω resistors are in series across 24V. What are the voltage drops?
options: 24V across each.
8V across 4Ω and 16V across 8Ω.
12V across each.
16V across 4Ω and 8V across 8Ω.
reasons: The full source voltage across each does not describe this series circuit.
This follows the conditions and decision procedure in the lesson.
Current is shared, but resistances differ.
At equal current, the larger resistance has the larger drop.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q01.stem: A practice result is theory 21/30 and practical 5/10. How is it assessed using this app’s equally weighted practice questions?
options: Both pass because the total is 26/40.
Theory meets its threshold; practical does not.
Surplus theory answers can cover practical.
Neither can be assessed from correct counts.
reasons: Separate thresholds cannot be replaced by a combined score.
Compare theory’s minimum 20 and practical’s minimum 6 separately.
Correct answers cannot transfer between sections.
This textbook specifies separate minimum counts.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q02.stem: You hear unusual vibration from a panel outside your responsibility. Which response fits your role?
options: Touch the energized interior to investigate.
Hide the discovery if the noise stops.
Make the situation safe under the approved procedure and report the equipment and observations.
A safety manager means workers need not report.
reasons: Unauthorized contact with energized parts is dangerous.
Information remains necessary even if it temporarily stops.
Respect roles and report observed facts.
Management arrangements do not replace individual reporting.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q03.stem: A terminal shelf has 5 against a lower limit of 8, and one wrong part. What should you do?
options: Move everything to another empty shelf.
The three fixed conditions concern location only.
Count the wrong item as specified stock.
Identify and report shortage and mixing separately after checking.
reasons: Moving alone resolves neither cause nor identity.
Item and quantity are also included.
A wrong item is not stock of the specified part.
Check deviations in both item and quantity.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q04.stem: You only watched a demonstration during OJT on a new machine. What must be checked before assignment?
options: Watching fulfills every statutory requirement.
One pair of gloves for all tasks is enough.
Try unknown controls alone.
Required education/qualifications, authorization scope, and understood procedures.
reasons: OJT does not automatically replace qualifications.
Gloves can be hazardous around rotation.
Resolve questions before starting.
OJT, requirements, and understanding are separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q05.stem: A site has signs for an evacuation building and a tsunami refuge. How do you choose?
options: Match disaster type with the workplace evacuation plan.
Both are always equivalent if green.
Walk opposite the arrows.
Evacuation locations are unnecessary if prohibitions are obeyed.
reasons: Location purpose and disaster conditions differ.
The same color does not establish the same target.
This contradicts directions.
Emergency routes also need checking.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q06.stem: A decanted cleaning liquid has no known product name, and the original container is missing. First response?
options: Smell a little to identify it.
Suspend use and ask for product identification and SDS confirmation.
No flame symbol means safe.
Mix it if the color matches the old liquid.
reasons: Smelling can cause exposure.
Identify first, then match hazard information.
A missing label is not evidence of safety.
Color does not establish composition or compatibility.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q07.stem: A part nearly fell this month without injury. How should 1:29:300 be used?
options: Serious accidents cannot occur before 300 events.
No injury means no record.
Treat it as a warning, report it, and assess measures; do not use counts as safety limits.
The ratio establishes the cause.
reasons: No count guarantees safety before it.
Near-miss information matters.
The ratio is a concept, not a predictive guarantee.
A count ratio cannot establish cause.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q08.stem: For a 65% threshold on 30 theory questions, what is the minimum correct count?
reasons: At least 19.5 means 20 as an integer.
19/30 is below 65%.
Do not calculate using 40 combined questions.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q09.stem: Shelf location and part number are right but stock exceeds the specified upper limit. Which condition is primarily violated?
options: Fixed location
Fixed quantity
Fixed item
Projection method
reasons: Location is correct.
The quantity range is exceeded.
Part number is correct.
Projection concerns drawings, not stock.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q10.stem: Is it acceptable to test a rotating machine before training because you have protective glasses?
options: No: protection, education, and authorization are separate checks.
Yes: protecting the eyes removes every hazard.
OJT equals all qualifications.
New work needs no startup check.
reasons: Several safety conditions must be met.
Entanglement and other dangers remain.
Requirements depend on the work.
Confirm startup checks.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q11.stem: Before reading an SDS, what information should first match?
options: Only paper color.
Only the former container shape.
Product identification on the container and SDS.
Only shelf height.
reasons: Color does not identify the product.
Different contents can use similar containers.
Another product’s SDS can have different requirements.
Location does not identify composition.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-07-q12.stem: New trip hazards increase a week after a safety measure. What is the OSHMS response?
options: Stop observing because implementation is complete.
Discard records.
Declare absolute safety.
Assess new risks and effectiveness, then revise the plan.
reasons: Implementation alone is not completion.
Comparison information would be lost.
This ignores a new hazard.
An evaluation/improvement cycle is necessary.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q01.stem: Material lot and tool changed when defects increased. What should quality investigation do?
options: Blame only the worker.
Skip inspection for delivery.
Compare facts through 4M, including material and machine changes.
Treat design and logistics quality as identical.
reasons: Other factors remain unchecked.
Do not lower safety or quality requirements.
Investigate multiple change points.
They concern different stages.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q02.stem: With matched inspection conditions, defects changed from 6/200 to 2/200. Which explanation is correct?
options: The difference 4 means 4%.
Stop assessing because defects fell.
Always touch energized items for actual-item checks.
The rate fell from 3%to 1%; assess other conditions too.
reasons: 4/200 is a 2-percentage-point difference.
Connect Check to Act.
The three actuals do not require dangerous touching.
Keep the denominator and other conditions in the assessment.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q03.stem: A drawing is revised but the QC process chart is old. What before starting?
options: Resolve the target/revision mismatch and align approved control conditions.
Halve frequency yourself.
A work standard makes QC conditions unnecessary.
Hide the old version and record it as new.
reasons: Check applicability and revision first.
Frequency changes require approval.
Instructions and controls have different roles.
Do not falsify records.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q04.stem: A scatterplot shows larger dimensions at higher temperatures. What can currently be said?
options: A relationship is observed; other conditions need checking before deciding cause.
Temperature alone is proven the sole cause.
A scatterplot is a time-series control-limit chart.
Correlation removes the need for data counts.
reasons: Correlation is not causation.
Other factors remain possible.
It plots paired variables.
Conditions and sample size remain necessary.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q05.stem: A dropped instrument has a JIS mark. How should its next use be decided?
options: The mark eliminates drop effects.
Organizational ISO certification automatically passes each result.
JIS and product inspection mean the same thing.
Check condition, calibration, and pre-use requirements, not the mark alone.
reasons: Damage or shift is possible.
Certification scope differs from individual results.
Standards conformity differs from inspection of the item.
Marking and present reliability are separate.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q06.stem: What is the calculated energy for 900 W used 20 minutes?
options: 300 Wh
900 Wh
reasons: Minutes were used directly as hours.
20 minutes=1/3 hour, so 900×1/3=300 Wh.
The duration is not one hour.
W is not an energy unit.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q07.stem: Equal-volume reference water has mass 40 g; material specific gravity is 2.7. What is its calculated mass?
reasons: The ratio is inverted.
Specific gravity cannot be added to mass.
The equal-volume water mass was not multiplied.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q08.stem: Drawing requirements were met but delivery was late. How should customer requirements be considered?
options: Performance alone satisfies every requirement.
Check both quality characteristics and delivery timing.
Delivery is not part of QCD.
Logistics has no relation to quality.
reasons: This ignores the commitment to the customer.
Requirements are not one-dimensional.
D means delivery.
Quality extends through delivery.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q09.stem: Which PDCA stage compares target and actual result?
options: Plan
Do only
Act only
Check
reasons: It sets goals and methods.
It implements.
It feeds evaluated results into improvement.
It evaluates results against the target.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q10.stem: A worker independently changed “once per lot” to “once per hour.” What is the problem?
options: Both always inspect the same quantity.
Equal wording length means equivalent conditions.
Control conditions were substituted without approval.
QC charts never state frequency.
reasons: Lot sizes can differ.
Text length is not a control condition.
Time and lots are different divisions.
Frequency is an important control item.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-08-q11.stem: “Tool wear” is written on a 4Mcause-and-effect diagram. What is its current status?
options: The confirmed sole cause.
A possible cause to verify.
Automatic approval to replace tools.
The correlation coefficient itself.
reasons: Writing it does not prove it.
Verify candidates with facts.
Change authorization is separate.
It is not a numerical relationship coefficient.

options: 2 m²
reasons: 1 mm²=10⁻⁶m², hence 2×10⁻⁶.
A length factor was directly used for area.
The conversion factor is wrong.
The unit difference was ignored.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q01.stem: How do returnable-box reuse and copper-offcut recovery differ?
options: The first is Reuse, the second Recycle.
Both only aim to increase waste.
Reuse means melting everything.
Recycling needs no separation or identification.
reasons: Distinguish using a product again from recovering resources.
This reverses 3R goals.
Resource recovery such as melting is different.
Different materials and hazards need sorting.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q02.stem: You want an unknown-specification AC adapter in a panel. How should checks be divided?
options: PSE authorizes every connection.
A breaker permits removing grounding.
Old product counts establish current coverage.
Check product coverage, installation suitability, and worker conditions separately.
reasons: A mark does not establish every use.
Do not decide omission conditions independently.
Check the applicable date and public guidance.
Product, installation, and work requirements are separate.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-09-q03.stem: An export specification states an IEC edition. How should a domestic part be chosen?

Run to the supply at the fire source.
reasons: Possessing an extinguisher does not restore a lost escape route; do not continue dangerously.
Initial firefighting requires a safe escape route and similar conditions, not dangerous approach.
Searching inside smoke delays evacuation and increases danger.
Running to the fire brings fire or shock exposure and is outside safe-position operation conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q10.stem: You are assigned to carry a heavy box. Which pre-start check is most suitable?
options: Check weight, shape, distance, route and specified assistance.
Practice until you can lift it alone.
Judge every hazard from one handling-posture point.
Take a shortcut under a suspended load.
reasons: Safe handling considers the method and surroundings as well as weight.
Do not force practice until you can lift alone; check weight and assistance first.
Posture alone does not check distance, route, shape and other hazards.
A shortcut under a suspended load has a falling-load hazard and is not a safe carrying route.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q11.stem: Only you received the updated procedure; the next operator still has the old version. What is needed?
options: Your knowledge alone completes the update.
Either version may be chosen freely.
Mix old conditions from memory.
Check effective date, target, old-version separation and communication.
reasons: Changes must reach the people concerned; your own knowledge is insufficient.
Free choice between versions of unclear applicability disrupts consistency.
Mixing versions from memory may follow neither approved procedure.
The update must reach the next operator correctly and make the applicable version clear.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-09-q12.stem: An unjudged item is in a box scheduled for shipment. What is suitable?
options: Ship because the date has arrived.
Remove its label and mix it with good items.
Keep it identified and separated, and ask quality staff.
Relax the criteria and pass it.
reasons: A shipping date does not establish an unjudged item as conforming.
Removing the label and mixing loses status and target identification, risking escape.
Prevent unconfirmed items leaving and obtain an authorized judgment.
There is no authority to relax the criteria, and doing so does not resolve the unjudged state.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q01.stem: Before approaching someone who may be receiving an electric shock, what is suitable?
options: Pull their hand to rescue them immediately.
Assume any nearby piece of wood is safe.
Touch to check whether electricity is present.
Do not touch directly; report and carry out possible stopping from a safe position.
reasons: Direct hand contact may expose the rescuer to shock.
A nearby wooden object may not meet the necessary conditions; do not approach an unknown energized state.
Checking electricity with the body itself creates shock danger.
Avoid secondary harm to the rescuer; do not contact an unknown energized state.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q02.stem: A circuit breaker repeatedly trips. What should happen before restart?
options: Keep resetting and running.
Report the conditions and obtain the responsible person’s cause and safety checks.
Disable protection.
Replace it with a higher rating without authorization.
reasons: Repeated resets without cause confirmation can re-energize an abnormal condition.
Do not keep resetting while the cause of protective operation remains unknown.
Disabling protection removes the ability to interrupt dangerous faults.
Replacement without checking required ratings or equipment conditions can defeat suitable protection.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q03.stem: Can any plastic sheet serve as protection for energized work?
options: No; check material conditions and its specification as protective equipment.
Yes; the material name guarantees safety.
Dirt and damage are irrelevant.
Performance is unlimited at high temperature.
reasons: Insulation performance depends on voltage, temperature, damage and related conditions.
The material name alone does not guarantee protection at the required voltage or condition.
Dirt and damage may affect insulation, so condition checks are necessary.
Temperature limits apply; performance is not necessarily maintained without limits in heat.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q04.stem: A device has stopped, so someone says its capacitor terminals may be touched with a tool. What should you do?
options: A stopped indication alone proves discharge.
Short the terminals to check.
Do not touch; have residual energy checked by designated personnel and procedures.
If it looks similar, treat it like a battery.
reasons: A stopped display does not prove stored energy has disappeared.
Independently shorting terminals is not a safe discharge-verification procedure.
Energy can remain after power is off, and unauthorized shorting is dangerous.
A capacitor and battery have different mechanisms; check the item’s specifications and handling.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q05.stem: You want to identify a part used for amplification or on/off control. Which explanation is suitable?
options: Check this as a transistor function.
A diode is only for amplification.
A capacitor always emits light.
Every similarly shaped part is identical.
reasons: Transistors are used for amplification or switching; match function and part number.
This confuses a diode’s one-direction conduction with transistor amplification and control.
A capacitor serves temporary storage and related functions; it is not necessarily a light-emitting part.
The same shape can conceal different functions, terminals or ratings.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q06.stem: In equal-weight practice scoring, theory is 19/30 and practical 10/10. What do the app’s independent conditions give?
options: 29/40 in total guarantees a pass.
Perfect practical marks remove the need for theory.
Judge by combining theory and practical times.
Theory misses the required 20, so both sections have not passed.
reasons: Even a high combined total does not meet the separate theory minimum.
Practical marks do not replace taking theory and meeting its minimum.
Managing time and deciding each section’s pass result are different conditions.
Practice requires at least 20 theory and 6 practical answers correct independently.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q07.stem: A study group proposes memorizing and sharing actual exam questions. How should you proceed?
options: A private group is always permitted.
Take out only part of the answers.
Use original general examples without collecting or recreating actual questions.
Share if the invigilator cannot see.
reasons: Avoid sharing actual questions or answers whether publicly or privately.
Even partial actual questions or answers must not be taken out or shared.
The source warns against taking out or sharing actual questions and answers.
Follow fair-exam and information rules, rather than basing conduct on visibility to an invigilator.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q08.stem: A ground wire is connected. May isolation checks for internal inspection be omitted?
options: Grounding removes every shock hazard.
No; follow the equipment-specific isolation and related procedures.
Disassemble based only on the switch indication.
Leakage itself can no longer occur.
reasons: Grounding is part of protection, not removal of all shock danger.
Grounding does not replace the safety procedure for internal work.
A stopped indication alone does not meet isolation checks needed for internal work.
Grounding does not necessarily prevent leakage itself from occurring.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q09.stem: Which matches equipment driving a pump with equipment changing voltage?
options: Both are circuit breakers only.
A motor only changes voltage.
A transformer necessarily produces hydraulic pressure.
A motor converts electricity to motion; a transformer changes voltage.
reasons: A breaker interrupts for protection; it does not replace both conversion functions.
A motor primarily converts electricity into mechanical power.
Transformer voltage conversion and hydraulic-pressure generation are different functions.
Distinguish motion, voltage conversion and protection.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q10.stem: Which material uses electrical properties that vary with heat, light and related conditions?
options: Rubber of universally identical performance
Cross-section shape alone
A semiconductor
Packaging-paper color
reasons: Calling all rubber identical does not describe a semiconductor’s condition-dependent properties.
Cross-section alone does not explain classification by heat- or light-dependent electrical behavior.
Semiconductors use condition-dependent properties in electronic parts and related applications.
Packaging-paper color does not establish a material’s semiconductor function.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q11.stem: An LED and another part share the same outline. What is needed before replacement?
options: Declare them interchangeable from outline alone.
Check drawing role, part number, terminals and ratings.
Try power; lighting is sufficient.
Reverse direction removes the need for rating checks.
reasons: An equal outline does not establish suitability for the drawing role, terminals or ratings.
Appearance alone does not establish compatible function, direction and ratings.
Trying power on an unknown part is not a safe method of selecting a suitable component.
Both direction and ratings require checking; reverse operation is not unconditionally permitted.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-10-q12.stem: You read only part of「してはいけない」and judged it as「してよい」. How should study improve?
options: Read through the ending, including conditions and negation, and check the situation and meaning.
Knowing technical terms makes endings unnecessary.
Fix unknown words’ meanings by guessing.
Never recheck after one reading.
reasons: Endings and conditions can reverse meaning, so read the whole statement.
Even known technical terms can be changed by sentence-ending negation or conditions.
Do not fix an unknown meaning by guessing; ask about the target and meaning.
Reading once does not guarantee understanding; recheck conditions and sentence endings.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q01.stem: A passage has “No running” and “Warning: step down” signs. What do they mean together?
options: Running lets you ignore the step.
Both prohibit drinking.
Running is prohibited, and a downward step is indicated.
The warning sign permits running.
reasons: Moving faster does not remove the fall hazard at a step.
Drinking prohibition and running or step hazards have different targets.
Read the prohibited action separately from the hazard being indicated.
A warning alongside a prohibition does not cancel the no-running rule.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q02.stem: A chemical label shows a fish and tree. What should you first understand?
options: It concerns harm to the aquatic environment; also check the label and SDS.
The liquid is drinkable.
It is for washing fish.
It has no health hazards at all.
reasons: It indicates possible harm to aquatic life or the environment; substance and control details need further checking.
An environmental-hazard symbol does not mean drinking is safe.
The fish picture does not identify a washing application.
Environmental-hazard information does not guarantee harmlessness to people.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q03.stem: Measures have been implemented under OSHMS. Which stage checks their effect?
options: Discard implementation records.
Stop hazard investigations forever.
Hide the goals.
Evaluate implementation and results.
reasons: Discarding records prevents tracing effectiveness.
Remaining hazards and changes still need checks after implementation.
Without the goal, achievement is hard to evaluate.
Compare actual results with goals and feed improvement.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q04.stem: How should hole-diameter readings and nonconforming-unit counts be classified?
options: Diameter is attribute data; counts are variable data.
Diameter is variable data; counts are attribute data.
Both are necessarily temperature.
Omit units and mix them in one field.
reasons: This reverses variable and attribute data.
Separate a continuously measured dimension from a counted number of items.
Dimensions and counts are not temperatures.
Mixing loses the meaning of measurements and counts.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q05.stem: Which hardness uses the long diagonal of an elongated diamond-shaped indentation?
options: Knoop hardness HK.
Rockwell indentation depth.
Shore rebound height.
Brinell ball-indentation diameter.
reasons: The source’s Knoop method uses the long diagonal of an elongated indentation.
Rockwell uses depth, not the requested long diagonal.
Shore uses rebound, not indentation-diagonal reading.
Brinell uses ball-indentation diameter, not a diamond-shaped diagonal.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q06.stem: A person trained in visual inspection wants to identify an unknown liquid by taste. Which judgment is suitable?
options: Taste is a sense, so every liquid may be tasted.
A small amount is always safe.
Do not taste; ask about identification and the specified inspection method.
No smell means it may be drunk.
reasons: A sensory category is not permission to put an unknown factory liquid into the mouth.
Safety of an unknown substance is not guaranteed even in a small amount.
A sensory classification does not permit exposure to unknown substances; safe targets and methods are needed.
Absence of odor does not prove safe drinking.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q07.stem: Which aid has a V-shaped groove supporting a cylinder?
options: An inside caliper only.
A V-block.
A display label.
A paint bath.
reasons: An inside caliper transfers dimensions and is not a V-groove support.
A V-groove supports cylinders and similar targets.
A label gives identification information; it does not hold the object.
A paint bath is not a measuring support aid.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q08.stem: What can be concluded from a “No smoking” sign?
options: All warnings may be ignored.
Every ignition source other than smoking is necessarily allowed.
Smoking once is acceptable.
Smoking at that place is prohibited.
reasons: One prohibition does not cancel other warnings.
No smoking alone does not authorize other ignition sources; check other instructions.
Even a single occurrence of the prohibited action is not allowed.
The sign prohibits the action of smoking.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q09.stem: There are directions to both a tsunami evacuation site and an extensive outdoor evacuation space. What should you do?
options: Always go to low outdoor ground for any disaster.
Choose distance from sign color alone.
Check the evacuation plan and route suitable for the disaster.
Different names always mean the same place.
reasons: Low outdoor ground is not necessarily safe during a tsunami.
Color alone does not establish the suitability of a route or destination.
Safe-site conditions may differ between a tsunami, fire and other disasters.
Do not treat differently named evacuation sites as identical without checking.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q10.stem: A lot has been rejected. How should sorting or return be decided?
options: Remove labels and ship.
Relax the criteria yourself.
Choose only convenient good items for the next sample.
Keep identification and obtain the quality staff’s instructions and approval.
reasons: Removing identification risks releasing rejected items.
Changing criteria is not the formal disposition of a rejected lot.
Arbitrary selection changes the specified sampling method.
Decide disposition under procedures and authority, keeping the target traceable.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q11.stem: Which hardness test uses the rebound height of a dropped hammer?
options: Shore.
Vickers square-pyramidal diagonals.
Knoop long diagonal.
Elongation after fracture in a tensile test.
reasons: This matches the source’s Shore rebound-height example.
Vickers uses an indentation, not rebound height.
Knoop uses an indentation’s long diagonal.
Tensile elongation after fracture is different from a rebound hardness test.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-11-q12.stem: Which aid fixes a measuring instrument with a magnet and holding structure?
options: A sample’s nonconforming-unit rate.
A magnetic base.
A thimble reading.
Tensile strength.
reasons: A nonconforming rate is an inspection-data ratio, not a fixture.
Magnetic fixing and holding are this aid’s functions.
A thimble is a micrometer reading component.
Tensile strength is a material property, not a fixture.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q01.stem: A CMM measured a hole position. How should surface roughness be recorded?
options: Copy the coordinates as Ra.
Check roughness separately with the specified parameter, location and conditions.
One touch confirms roughness over the entire surface.
Pass roughness from the instrument name alone.
reasons: Coordinates and Ra represent different quantities.
Position and microscopic surface unevenness are different requirements; a roughness result is needed.
A single contact does not measure roughness over the entire surface.
The instrument name is not a result for the target area.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q02.stem: A gauge-block measuring face is damaged. What should you do?
options: Refinish it with an ordinary file.
Wring it with dirty paper between the faces.
A reference cannot be affected by damage.
Withhold use and check condition and impact through the designated procedure.
reasons: Independent repair with an ordinary file damages precision measuring faces.
Foreign matter means the specified reference length is no longer established.
Reference instruments also require damage and condition checks.
A damaged reference may affect later comparisons, so prescribed verification is needed.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q03.stem: A thin double-dash-dot line shows a reference tool position. How should it be read?
options: Distinguish it from the actual outline and identify the reference position.
Always cut material to that line.
It always outlines a hole.
Line type is irrelevant.
reasons: A phantom line can indicate reference shapes or positions.
A reference position must not be machined as the finished outline.
Do not unconditionally interpret double-dash-dot lines as hole outlines.
Line type identifies the role of a shape or instruction.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q04.stem: What is the distinction between Sφ 8 and SR 8?
options: Both are thickness 8.
Both give the same sphere size.
Sphere diameter 8 and sphere radius 8.
A 45-degree chamfer 8 and depth 8.
reasons: Thickness uses t and related notation, not the sphere symbols.
A sphere of radius 8 has diameter 16, so the sizes are not identical.
Sφmeans sphere diameter and SR sphere radius; equal numbers specify different sizes.
Do not reinterpret sphere dimensions as chamfers or depths.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q05.stem: Roundness was checked at one section. What about the whole cylindrical form?
options: One circular section guarantees the entire length.
Replace it with a length value.
Move the reference wherever you like.
Separately check cylindricity and related requirements and perform the needed measurements.
reasons: One circular section does not guarantee cylindrical form over the length.
Length conformity is different from conformity of cylindrical form.
Do not independently change the required reference or target.
A circle and an entire cylinder are different evaluation targets.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q06.stem: A part must release heat quickly, but only density was compared. What further view is needed?
options: Packaging-paper color alone.
Thermal conductivity, required function and service conditions.
Luster makes melting point irrelevant.
Light materials always transmit heat well.
reasons: Packaging color does not indicate material thermal conductivity.
Ease of transmitting heat is a physical property separate from density.
Shine does not establish suitability for temperature conditions or melting behavior.
Low mass and thermal conductivity are different properties and do not necessarily track each other.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q07.stem: The area around a weld did not melt. How should its properties be judged?
options: No melting means its structure can never change.
Surface color guarantees all strength properties.
Check the necessary range and evaluation as a heat-affected zone.
Forging flow lines and a welding reference line are the same.
reasons: Structural change from heat can occur while material remains solid.
Color does not replace the required strength test or inspection.
Heat can change structure or properties outside the melted zone.
Internal material flow and a drawing reference line are different concepts.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q08.stem: Which part traces the surface in a stylus roughness instrument?
options: The stylus.
A packaging label.
Lathe soft jaws.
An evacuation-site sign.
reasons: Stylus movement becomes a signal used to examine unevenness.
A label supplies identification; it is not a stylus.
Soft jaws hold a workpiece.
A sign guides action; it is not a measuring contact.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q09.stem: Someone wants to change a C2 chamfer instruction to R2. Which judgment is suitable?
options: Both use 2, so the machining is identical.
The shape requirements differ, so do not change it without authorization.
C necessarily means sphere radius.
R means thickness, so there is no problem.
reasons: The auxiliary symbol changes the requirement even if the number is the same.
A C 45-degree chamfer and an R rounded form are different shapes.
Sphere radius uses SRand related notation, not C.
R means radius, different from thickness t.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q10.stem: A drawing specifies parallelism and position. Which combination should be checked?
options: Each characteristic, target, tolerance value and necessary reference.
Use only the larger number for both.
Passing one confirms both.
Read every symbol as roundness.
reasons: Follow orientation and position relationships separately for each indication.
Combining different characteristics into one value loses requirements.
One characteristic’s result does not replace measurement of the other.
Parallelism, position and roundness are different characteristics.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q11.stem: Which is suitable storage after using gauge blocks?
options: Leave fingerprints and put them in water.
Mix them with ordinary offcuts.
Press measuring faces onto the floor.
Remove dirt and fingerprints and follow specified rust prevention and storage.
reasons: Fingerprints and inappropriate moisture can cause rust and related problems.
Mixing with offcuts can cause damage or mistaken selection.
Floor contact can damage or contaminate a measuring face.
Protect precision faces and maintain their condition as future references.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-12-q12.stem: What is the source’s relative thin:thick:extra-thick line-weight ratio?
options: Line types need not be read.
reasons: This reverses the relative sizes of thin and extra-thick lines.
This makes all three weights identical.
The source gives the relative line-weight ratio as 1:2:4.
Check line types and purposes together with weight.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q01.stem: Which part grips a workpiece on the lathe diagram?
options: An evacuation sign.
The roughness parameter Ra.
Variable data.
The chuck.
reasons: A sign is not a lathe workholding component.
Ra is a roughness parameter, not a machine part.
Variable data is a classification, not a holding-part name.
A chuck is associated with workpiece holding.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q02.stem: Which machine in the source changes tools automatically?
options: A box fixture block only.
A machining center.
An inside caliper only.
An AED.
reasons: A box fixture block aids fixing; it is not an automatic tool-changing machine.
A machining center is an example with automatic tool changing.
An inside caliper helps transfer dimensions and similar information.
An AED is an emergency medical device, not a machine tool.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q03.stem: After stopping, you must clear sharp chips. What is suitable?
options: Check safety and use the specified brush or tool.
Grip them with bare hands.
Restart rotation to throw them away.
Assume they are cool if they shine.
reasons: Consider sharpness and heat, using specified tools and the stopping procedure.
Sharp chips can injure hands.
Restarting to scatter chips increases contact and flying-material hazards.
Luster does not establish a safe temperature.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q04.stem: Someone wants to remove every reinforcing fiber from reinforced plastic as contamination. Which judgment is suitable?
options: All fibers are necessarily defects.
The resin name is unchanged, so performance is identical.
This changes the specified composition; do not remove fibers independently.
Removing air with a roller is metal cutting.
reasons: Intentional reinforcing fibers are different from foreign matter.
Presence or absence of reinforcement changes properties, so equal performance cannot be assumed.
Keep the specified composition combining reinforcement with resin.
Air removal belongs to resin forming, not material-removal machining.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q05.stem: Which process puts a product in a bath and uses electricity to form a paint film?
options: Electrodeposition coating.
Brush painting.
Always the same as electrostatic painting attracting charged particles through air.
Rolling.
reasons: This describes electrodeposition using electricity in a bath.
Brushing spreads paint with a tool rather than depositing it in a bath.
Its paint-supply process and mechanism differ from electrostatic painting.
Rolling deforms material with rolls.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q06.stem: Cold rolling caused work hardening. Which process should be checked to soften the material?
options: Quenching and annealing are merely names, so choose freely.
Correct thickness makes later processes unnecessary.
Unlimited rolling oil always restores the properties.
The specified annealing or other post-treatment.
reasons: The purposes and conditions differ, so these treatments are not freely interchangeable.
Thickness and material hardness are separate requirements.
More oil does not replace an approved property-adjusting treatment.
Check post-treatment against its purpose and process sheet.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q07.stem: An aluminum-extruded heat-dissipation part has many thin fins. What is their purpose?
options: Only reducing packaging quantity.
Making melting point infinite.
Increasing surface area to help release heat.
Omitting every strength inspection.
reasons: Fins are a part feature, not merely a determinant of packaging quantity.
A shape change does not make melting point infinite.
The source’s fin shape corresponds to the heat-dissipation purpose.
Knowing a shape’s purpose does not remove necessary strength or other checks.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q08.stem: A learner identifies soft jaws and wants to check their mounting by hand during operation. What is suitable?
options: Knowing the name permits touching during operation.
Do not touch; check stopping, training and procedures.
Soft jaws cannot cause entanglement.
The tailstock is a sign and irrelevant.
reasons: Knowing a name does not make contact with rotating parts safe.
Identifying a part does not replace practical authority or safety checks.
Soft jaw material does not remove the danger of a rotating workholding part.
A tailstock is a lathe support component, not a sign.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q09.stem: A grinding wheel may be cracked. What should you do?
options: High speed closes cracks.
Push hard against its side as a test.
Protective glasses make inspection unnecessary.
Withhold use and obtain specified inspection and responsible-person checks.
reasons: High speed does not prove a crack safe and can lead to breakage.
Unauthorized side use or force-testing does not establish suitability.
Protection does not replace wheel-condition inspection.
Fragments can fly at high speed, so the prescribed condition check is necessary.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q10.stem: Distinguish a long constant-section tube from a hollow container inflated in a mold. Which combination fits?
options: Both are necessarily rolled.
Both are metal tempering.
Extrusion as a candidate, and blow molding as a candidate.
Every material solidifies the same way.
reasons: Rolling uses rolls, unlike the described resin processes.
Tempering is a heat treatment for steel and similar materials, not resin forming.
Distinguish a continuing cross-section from an air-inflation process.
Cooling and reaction curing involve different ways of becoming solid.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q11.stem: A hot-rolled product was measured while hot. What should be considered for its cooled dimensions?
options: The hot value always equals the cooled value.
Check thermal dimensional change and the specified measurement state.
An oxide film guarantees dimensions.
Heating needs no energy.
reasons: Dimensions can change with temperature.
Cooling can cause shrinkage, so match comparison conditions.
An oxide film is not a guarantee of dimensional conformity; it is also a surface-check target.
Heating requires energy.

mfg1-mechanical-weekly-13-q12.stem: Someone wants to omit cooling, straightening and cutting after extrusion, accepting the product from length alone. What is suitable?
options: Check completion of later processes and inspection against the process sheet and requirements.
Passing the die meets every requirement.
Fix the source’s heating example as every material’s setting.
Stop the hot product by hand to check.
reasons: Processes may still be needed to establish condition and dimensions as well as extruded shape.
A formed cross-section is not completion if cooling, straightening or other requirements remain unfinished.
A heating example is not a common instruction for all materials and equipment.
Reaching for a moving or hot product creates contact and related hazards.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q01.stem: Someone proposes fixing one button of a two-hand control and operating only the other. What hazard explanation is appropriate?
options: An emergency stop makes two-hand operation unnecessary.
Faster starting prevents entanglement.
The machine may operate with the freed hand in the danger area.
People behind the machine face no hazard.
reasons: An emergency stop does not replace guarding or operating conditions.
Speed does not prevent entry into a hazard area.
Fixing one button removes the condition keeping both hands at the controls.
Approaching third parties may also be crushed.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q02.stem: A drawing has phantom lines for another position of a moving part and hatching for a section. Which explanation is appropriate?
options: Phantom lines indicate motion positions; hatching indicates section areas.
Every phantom line indicates dimensional tolerance.
Machine both as solid outlines.
Hatching always indicates electrical continuity.
reasons: Distinguish their purposes when reading drawing information.
Read tolerances from separate dimension specifications.
Their purposes differ from visible outlines.
Hatching indicates sections or specified areas, not electrical continuity.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q03.stem: An automatic-return pushbutton and maintained emergency-stop actuator were assumed identical. What should be reassessed?
options: A round shape always returns automatically.
Contact shape certifies the entire machine’s safety.
Erase identifiers and use order to identify them.
Check holding and release conditions against symbols and specifications.
reasons: Shape alone does not establish return behavior.
Whole-system safety is not established by contact shape.
Identifiers and specifications are needed to identify behavior.
Actuation and return require separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q04.stem: Under equal length, area and temperature, textbook resistivities are1/58 for annealed copper and1/35 for aluminum. Which is correct?
options: Aluminum’s low mass necessarily means lower resistivity.
Annealed copper has lower resistivity in this comparison.
Density and resistivity are identical quantities.
1/58 is larger, so copper resistance is larger.
reasons: Low mass and conductivity are separate properties.
Resistance is proportional to resistivity under equal conditions.
Density relates mass to volume.
The fractions are reversed in magnitude:1/58 is smaller.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q05.stem: A nonmetal plate’s drawing specifies a flat washer, but none is in the parts box. What should you do?
options: Ignore part-number differences if the screw head fits.
Do not omit it; verify configuration and supply before tightening.
Double torque to compensate.
A spring washer always eliminates the flat washer.
reasons: Head fit alone does not establish conformity.
Do not change the specified assembly independently.
Excess torque does not replace a missing washer.
The two washers’ roles and specifications differ.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q06.stem: When a feed handle was reversed, play created a range over which motion was not transmitted. What is this play called?
options: Surface roughness
Thread pitch
Feed speed
Backlash
reasons: Roughness is fine surface unevenness, not feed play.
Pitch is the axial distance between corresponding points on adjacent threads, not mechanism play.
Feed speed is movement per time, not a play dimension.
Reversal play in motion transmission is backlash.

mfg1-electrical-weekly-13-q07.stem: A screw advances0.5 mm per turn and its thimble has50 divisions. What is one division?
options: 0.5 mm
25 mm
reasons: This divides by10 rather than50.
0.5 mm is the whole turn’s advance.
Multiplying0.5×50 does not divide the turn.

options: Follow standards while discussing hazards and advancing approved measures.
Remove safety devices according to personal preference.
Keep known hazards unshared.
Prioritize speed alone over procedures.
reasons: Combine standards compliance with self-directed improvement.
Voluntary activity does not authorize device removal.
Without sharing, hazards do not lead to measures.
Speed alone does not meet safety standards.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q02.stem: You heard about another factory's safety-and-health structure. What is appropriate for your workplace?
options: Assume identical staffing is required everywhere.
Check industry/size conditions and workplace roles and contacts.
Specialists mean workers need not follow standards.
Greeting frequency alone determines the structure.
reasons: Appointment and establishment conditions are not necessarily uniform.
Check applicable conditions and the actual structure.
Specialists do not exempt workers from compliance.
Greeting counts are not legal organizational conditions.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q03.stem: Immediately after greeting someone in a passage, you notice a leak. What is appropriate?
options: Do not report because the greeting is complete.
Wait for the other person to notice.
Take the prescribed safe response and specifically report location and condition.
Approach the leaked liquid to greet them.
reasons: A greeting alone does not communicate leak information.
Communicate specifics rather than waiting for guesses.
Safe response and a specific report are needed.
This increases potential contact.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q04.stem: There is sudden danger, but the safety committee meets next week. What is appropriate?
options: Continue work until the meeting.
An agenda entry eliminates emergency communication.
Check only other factories' schedules.
Follow workplace emergency communication, stopping and evacuation procedures.
reasons: A meeting schedule does not justify delayed immediate action.
Future deliberation and current emergency response are different.
This does not address the present danger.
Use the prescribed emergency procedures for sudden danger.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q05.stem: Which reading of specific gravity in Table 7-1 is correct?
options: Always add A to specific gravity.
Read a dimensionless ratio without guessing unlisted temperature conditions.
Treat the number as a melting point.
Assume every alloy has the same value.
reasons: A is a current unit.
Respect the meaning and limits of the table's conditions.
Specific gravity and melting point are different properties.
Composition and condition differences cannot be ignored.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q06.stem: Table 7-1 lists platinum 21.45 and aluminium 2.7. Which equal-volume paper comparison is appropriate?
options: Platinum always has the smaller mass.
Different specific gravities still give equal mass.
Platinum has the larger mass.
Equal volume eliminates material checks.
reasons: The specific-gravity ordering is reversed.
At equal volume, density affects mass.
This is valid when using the table's reference values.
Mass comparison is not an actual-material guarantee.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q07.stem: What follows from bismuth's low melting point description in Table 7-1?
options: Its exact melting point is 9.8°C.
Every alloy melts at the same temperature.
Heating tests are freely permitted.
It is qualitative; the table provides no numeric melting point.
reasons: 9.8 is specific gravity, not melting point.
It does not guarantee alloy melting points.
A property description does not authorize heating.
Separate the specific-gravity and property columns.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q08.stem: Nickel uses in Table 7-1 include stainless steel and alloys. What is appropriate?
options: These are representative applications, not grounds for unauthorized substitution.
Every steel has the same properties as pure nickel.
An example permits ignoring drawings.
Corrosion resistance alone guarantees every environment.
reasons: Separate examples from guarantees of product suitability.
Alloy and element properties need not match.
Compare suitability with drawings and controlled information.
Corrosion resistance has environmental and other conditions.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q09.stem: Table 7-2 lists copper 59.6 with heading 10⁶ S/m. Which value is correct?
options: It must mean 59.6%.
reasons: This omits the heading's 10⁶.
This reverses the multiplier.
The table uses S/m, not percentages.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q10.stem: Table 7-2 lists silver 62.1 and titanium 2.38. Which comparison is appropriate?
options: Titanium has higher conductivity.
Their conductivities match.
Silver has higher conductivity.
Silver eliminates terminal rating checks.
reasons: The value ordering is reversed.
The values differ.
Compare using the same table unit.
Conductivity alone does not determine safe terminal ratings.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q11.stem: Which relationship between conductivity and resistivity is correct?
options: They always have the same number and unit.
Conductivity is measured in Ω·m.
Resistivity is unrelated to conductivity.
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity.
reasons: They are different quantities.
Ω·m is the resistivity unit.
They have a reciprocal relationship.
Relate this to conductivity's S/m unit.

mfg1-surface-supplement-11-q12.stem: Convert conductivity 1 mS/m to S/m. Which result is correct?
options: It becomes only 1 S.
reasons: m means one thousandth; retain the length denominator.
The multiplier is reversed.
This confuses m and M.
Do not drop conductivity's/m.
